title_patterns: We Looked Through [Large Specific Number] of [Data Type]. [Surprising Comparison].
hook_patterns: Open with a named authority figure's exact quote or action before any commentary
Lead with one unrounded, specific data point (a %, a dollar figure, a trade count) instead of a general claim
Frame as direct comparison between two known entities ('X is doing more of this than Y')
Pose the video as answering one narrow, already-in-progress question rather than predicting doom
State the structural/legislative mechanism (bill, hearing, disclosure) before the market reaction
packaging_notes: Duration is bimodal: sub-3-minute clips win on breaking political/regulatory news (congressional trading, hearings), while 15-25 minute videos win on analytical deep-dives (bubble/crash explainers) — very little mid-length (5-10 min) content is breaking out.
Numbers are used for credibility, not shock — specific unrounded figures (20,000 trades, 44%, $200k) outperform vague superlatives; avoid rounded dramatic claims.

Recurring institutional/legislative angle (Congress stock-trading bans, insider trading bills) is repeatable across multiple channels and even re-uploads of near-identical titles, suggesting a durable structural news hook rather than a one-off story.
Multi-ticker 'earnings alert' listicle format performs consistently in short/mid runtime even at lower absolute views, showing niche utility content still outliers relative to channel baseline.

Same underlying story (e.g., a national market event) is being reframed as both a fast news-bite and a longer explainer by different channels — packaging duration should match how much original analysis vs. pure reporting is being offered.
